parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.lead: A sealed container of fixed volume *V* contains *N* molecules, each of mass *m*, of an ideal gas at pressure *p*.
parts.text: State an expression, in terms of *V*, *N*, *p* and the Boltzmann constant *k*, for the thermodynamic temperature *T* of the gas.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
Show that the mean translational kinetic energy *E*ₖ of a molecule of the gas is given by

$E_\mathrm{K} = \frac{3}{2}kT$.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text: Explain why the internal energy of the gas is equal to the total kinetic energy of the molecules.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.lead: The gas in (b) is supplied with thermal energy *Q*.
parts.text: Explain, with reference to the first law of thermodynamics, why the increase in internal energy of the gas is *Q*.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text:
Use the expression in (b)(ii) and the information in (c)(i) to show that the specific heat capacity *c* of the gas is given by

$c = \frac{3k}{2m}$.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
The container in (b) is now replaced with one that does not have a fixed volume. Instead, the gas is able to expand, so that the pressure of the gas remains constant as thermal energy is supplied.

Suggest, with a reason, how the specific heat capacity of the gas would now compare with the value in (c)(ii).
